metadata.title: Robust Stochastic Approximation Approach to Stochastic Programming
metadata.source_note: Extracted from PDF->text fallback; .tex source not available. Math fidelity reduced.

nodes.name: Stochastic optimization problem (1.1)
nodes.statement: $\min_{x \in X} \{ f(x) = \mathbb{E}[F(x,\xi)] \}$, with $X \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ nonempty bounded closed convex, $\xi$ a random vector on $\Xi \subset \mathbb{R}^d$, and $f$ continuous and convex on $X$.
nodes.statement_clean: Minimize over a convex compact set the expected value of a function of a random parameter.

nodes.name: (A1) IID sampling oracle
nodes.statement: It is possible to generate an iid sample $\xi_1, \xi_2, \ldots$ of realizations of the random vector $\xi$.

nodes.name: (A2) Stochastic subgradient oracle
nodes.statement: An oracle returns $G(x,\xi)$ such that $g(x) := \mathbb{E}[G(x,\xi)]$ is well-defined and $g(x) \in \partial f(x)$.

nodes.name: Nonexpansive projection (1.5)
nodes.statement: $\| \Pi_X(x') - \Pi_X(x) \|_2 \le \| x' - x \|_2$ for all $x', x \in \mathbb{R}^n$, where $\Pi_X$ is metric projection onto $X$.

nodes.name: Classical SA algorithm
nodes.statement: Subgradient-style stochastic approximation using projection onto $X$ at each iteration with stepsizes $\gamma_j$.
output: Iterates $x_j \in X$ approximating the minimizer $x_*$ of $f$ on $X$

nodes.name: Bounded second moment of stochastic subgradient (2.5)
nodes.statement: $\mathbb{E}[\| G(x, \xi) \|_2^2] \le M^2$ for all $x \in X$.

nodes.name: Strong convexity of $f$ (2.7)
nodes.statement: $(x' - x)^T (\nabla f(x') - \nabla f(x)) \ge c \| x' - x \|_2^2$ for all $x', x \in X$, with constant $c > 0$.

nodes.name: $O(t^{-1})$ convergence of classical SA under strong convexity
nodes.statement: Under (A1), (A2), strong convexity of $f$ with constant $c$, and stepsizes $\gamma_j = \theta/j$ with $\theta > 1/(2c)$: $\mathbb{E}\| x_j - x_* \|_2^2 \le Q(\theta)/j$ where $Q(\theta) = \max\{ \theta^2 M^2 (2c\theta - 1)^{-1}, \| x_1 - x_* \|_2^2 \}$.
assumptions: $f$ is differentiable and strongly convex on $X$ with constant $c > 0$
conclusions: If $x_*$ is interior and $\nabla f$ is Lipschitz with constant $L$: $\mathbb{E}[f(x_j) - f(x_*)] \le \tfrac{1}{2} L Q(\theta)/j$ (eq. (2.13))

nodes.name: Sensitivity of classical SA to overestimating $c$
nodes.statement: If the strong-convexity parameter $c$ is overestimated and stepsizes $\gamma_j = 1/j$ are used while the true $c = 0.2$, the classical SA converges as slowly as $x_j > 0.8 j^{-1/5}$, illustrating non-robustness of $\gamma_j = O(1/j)$.

nodes.name: Robust Euclidean SA (E-SA) with averaging
nodes.statement: Robust SA: run recurrence (2.1) with constant or $O(t^{-1/2})$ stepsizes, and report a weighted average of iterates as the approximate solution.
input: Stochastic subgradient oracle $G(x,\xi)$ satisfying $\mathbb{E}\| G \|_2^2 \le M^2$

nodes.name: $O(N^{-1/2})$ efficiency of Robust E-SA
nodes.statement: With constant stepsize $\gamma_t = \theta D_X / (M \sqrt{N})$, the averaged iterate satisfies $\mathbb{E}[f(\tilde{x}^N_K) - f(x_*)] \le \max\{\theta, \theta^{-1}\} \, D_X M / \sqrt{N} \cdot (2N/(N-K+1) + 1/2)$ for $1 \le K \le N$.
conclusions: Rate $O(N^{-1/2})$ holds without smoothness or strong convexity

nodes.name: Distance-generating function and its modulus
nodes.statement:
A function $\omega : X 	o \mathbb{R}$ is a distance-generating function modulus $\alpha > 0$ w.r.t. $\| \cdot \|$ if $\omega$ is convex, continuous, $X^o = \{ x \in X : \partial \omega(x) 
eq \emptyset \}$ is convex, and $\omega$ is continuously differentiable and strongly convex with parameter $\alpha$ on $X^o$: $(x' - x)^T(
abla \omega(x') - 
abla \omega(x)) \ge \alpha \| x' - x \|^2$.

nodes.name: Prox-function (Bregman distance)
nodes.statement: $V(x, z) = \omega(z) - \omega(x) - \nabla \omega(x)^T (z - x)$, defined for $x \in X^o$, $z \in X$; nonnegative and strongly convex in $z$ modulus $\alpha$ w.r.t. $\| \cdot \|$.

nodes.name: Prox-mapping
nodes.statement: $P_x(y) = \arg\min_{z \in X} \{ y^T(z - x) + V(x, z) \}$, the prox-mapping associated with $\omega$ at $x \in X^o$.

nodes.name: $\omega$-diameter $D_{\omega,X}$
nodes.statement: $D_{\omega,X} := (\max_{z \in X} \omega(z) - \min_{z \in X} \omega(z))^{1/2}$ (eq. (2.43)).

nodes.name: Mirror descent SA algorithm
nodes.statement: Generalization of E-SA replacing Euclidean projection by a prox-mapping derived from a distance-generating function $\omega$ adapted to the geometry of $X$.
input: Bounded closed convex $X \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ with norm $\| \cdot \|$ and dual $\| \cdot \|_*$
Stochastic subgradient oracle $G(x,\xi)$ with $\mathbb{E}\| G(x,\xi) \|_*^2 \le M_*^2$
nodes.pseudocode: Iterate $x_{j+1} = P_{x_j}(\gamma_j G(x_j, \xi_j))$ (eq. (2.32)), where $P_x(y) = \arg\min_{z \in X}\{ y^T(z-x) + V(x,z) \}$; return weighted average of iterates.

nodes.name: Lemma 2.1 (Prox-mapping inequality)
nodes.statement: For every $u \in X$, $x \in X^o$, and $y \in \mathbb{R}^n$: $V(P_x(y), u) \le V(x, u) + y^T(u - x) + \| y \|_*^2 / (2\alpha)$ (eq. (2.33)).
assumptions: $\omega$ is a distance-generating function modulus $\alpha$ w.r.t. $\| \cdot \|$

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2.1
nodes.statement: Use optimality of $v = P_x(y)$, the identity $V(v,u) - V(x,u) = (\nabla \omega(v) - \nabla \omega(x) + y)^T(v-u) + y^T(u-v)$, Young's inequality $y^T(x-v) \le \| y \|_*^2/(2\alpha) + (\alpha/2) \| x - v \|^2$, and strong convexity $V(x,v) \ge (\alpha/2) \| x - v \|^2$.

nodes.name: Mirror descent SA efficiency estimate
nodes.statement: With $x_1 = \arg\min_X \omega$ and constant stepsize $\gamma_t = \theta \sqrt{2 \alpha} D_{\omega,X} / (M_* \sqrt{N})$: $\mathbb{E}[f(\tilde{x}^N_1) - f(x_*)] \le \max\{\theta, \theta^{-1}\} \, D_{\omega,X} M_* \sqrt{2 / (\alpha N)}$ (eq. (2.48)).

nodes.name: Proposition 2.2 (Large deviations bound for mirror descent SA)
nodes.statement: Under the light-tail assumption $\mathbb{E}\exp\{ \| G(x,\xi) \|_*^2 / M_*^2 \} \le \exp\{1\}$ and constant stepsizes (2.47), for any $\Omega \ge 1$: $\Pr\{ f(\tilde{x}^N_1) - f(x_*) > \sqrt{2}\max\{\theta,\theta^{-1}\} M_* D_{\omega,X} (12 + 2\Omega) / \sqrt{\alpha N} \} \le 2 \exp\{-\Omega\}$.
assumptions: Light-tail condition (2.50): $\mathbb{E}\exp\{ \| G(x,\xi) \|_*^2 / M_*^2 \} \le e$ for all $x \in X$
conclusions: $\Pr\{ f(\tilde{x}^N_1) - f(x_*) > \sqrt{2}\max\{\theta,\theta^{-1}\} M_* D_{\omega,X} (12 + 2\Omega)/\sqrt{\alpha N} \} \le 2 e^{-\Omega}$

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 2.2
nodes.statement: Adapt the proof of Proposition 3.2 using the bound (2.39) in place of relations (6.5) and (6.7); details deferred in paper.

nodes.name: Mirror descent SA on the standard simplex: Euclidean vs. $\ell_1$ setup
nodes.statement: On $X = \{ x \in \mathbb{R}^n : \sum x_i = 1, x \ge 0 \}$, the $\ell_1$ setup (entropy $\omega(x) = \sum x_i \ln x_i$) gives $\mathbb{E}[f(\tilde{x}^N_1) - f(x_*)] \le O(1)\max\{\theta,\theta^{-1}\} \sqrt{\ln n} M_* / \sqrt{N}$, potentially much smaller than the Euclidean bound $O(M / \sqrt{N})$ since $M_*/M$ can be as small as $n^{-1/2}$.

nodes.name: Entropy distance-generating function on the simplex (2.58)
nodes.statement: $\omega(x) = \sum_{i=1}^n x_i \ln x_i$ (entropy), with $X^o = \{ x \in X : x > 0 \}$, $D_{\omega,X} = \sqrt{\ln n}$, $\alpha = 1$, $x_1 = n^{-1}(1, \ldots, 1)^T$.

nodes.name: Closed-form prox-mapping for entropy setup
nodes.statement: $[P_x(y)]_i = x_i e^{-y_i} / \sum_{k=1}^{n} x_k e^{-y_k}$, $i = 1, \ldots, n$ (computable in $O(n)$ operations).

nodes.name: Alternative $\ell_1$ distance-generating function (2.61)
nodes.statement: $\omega(x) = (\ln n) \sum_{i=1}^{n} | x_i |^{1 + 1/\ln n}$ for $n \ge 3$; with $0 \in X$ and $\mathrm{Diam}_{\| \cdot \|_1}(X) = 1$, $D_{\omega, X} = O(1)\sqrt{\ln n}$ and $\alpha = O(1)$.

nodes.name: Sample complexity comparison: SA vs. SAA
nodes.statement: Under light-tail conditions, $N_{SA} = O(1)\varepsilon^{-2} D_{\omega,X}^2 M_*^2 \ln^2(1/\delta)$ (eq. (2.64)) while $N_{SAA} = O(1)\varepsilon^{-2} R^2 M_*^2 [\ln(1/\delta) + n \ln(R M_*/\varepsilon)]$ (eq. (2.65)); both quadratic in $1/\varepsilon$ and logarithmic in $\delta$.

nodes.name: Stochastic convex-concave saddle point problem (3.1)
nodes.statement: $\min_{x \in X} \max_{y \in Y} \{ \phi(x,y) = \mathbb{E}[\Phi(x,y,\xi)] \}$, with $X \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ and $Y \subset \mathbb{R}^m$ nonempty bounded closed convex, $\phi$ convex in $x$ and concave in $y$, Lipschitz on $X \times Y$.

nodes.name: (A'2) Stochastic subgradient oracle for saddle point
nodes.statement: Oracle returns $G(x,y,\xi) = (G_x(x,y,\xi); -G_y(x,y,\xi))$ such that $g(x,y) = (g_x(x,y); -g_y(x,y)) = \mathbb{E}[G]$ has $g_x(x,y) \in \partial_x \phi(x,y)$ and $-g_y(x,y) \in \partial_y(-\phi(x,y))$.

nodes.name: Saddle point mirror SA algorithm
nodes.statement: Mirror SA recurrence in the joint variable $z = (x,y)$ with prox-mapping derived from a product distance-generating function on $Z = X \times Y$.
input: Stochastic subgradient oracle $G(x,y,\xi)$ with $\mathbb{E}\| G \|_*^2 \le M_*^2$
nodes.pseudocode: Iterate $z_{j+1} = P_{z_j}(\gamma_j G(z_j, \xi_j))$ (eq. (3.7)); return weighted average $\tilde{z}^j_1$ (eq. (3.8)).

nodes.name: Lemma 3.1 (Saddle-point error bound)
nodes.statement: For any $j \ge 1$: $\mathbb{E}[\max_{z \in Z} \sum_{t=1}^{j} \gamma_t (z_t - z)^T g(z_t)] \le 2 + \tfrac{5}{2} M_*^2 \sum_{t=1}^{j} \gamma_t^2$ (eq. (3.10)).

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3.1
nodes.statement: Apply Lemma 2.1 to obtain (6.2); sum to get (6.3) and decompose into deterministic and martingale parts; bound the martingale part via Lemma 6.1 and (6.6); take expectations and supremum to obtain (3.10).

nodes.name: Apply Lemma 2.1 in saddle setting
nodes.statement: By Lemma 2.1 applied with $u \in Z$, $x = z_t$, $y = \gamma_t G(z_t,\xi_t)$: $\gamma_t (z_t - u)^T G(z_t,\xi_t) \le V(z_t, u) - V(z_{t+1}, u) + (\gamma_t^2 / 2) \| G(z_t,\xi_t) \|_*^2$ (eq. (6.2)).

nodes.name: Introduce noise term $\Delta_t$ and rewrite
nodes.statement: Let $\Delta_t = G(z_t, \xi_t) - g(z_t)$; rewrite (6.2) as (6.3) splitting into deterministic gradient term and noise term.

nodes.name: Auxiliary sequence and Lemma 6.1
nodes.statement: Introduce auxiliary sequence $v_{t+1} = P_{v_t}(-\gamma_t \Delta_t)$ and apply Lemma 6.1 to bound $\sum_t \gamma_t \Delta_t^T(u - v_t)$ uniformly in $u \in Z$.

nodes.name: Bound expected supremum via $\mathbb{E}\| \Delta_t \|_*^2 \le 4 M_*^2$
nodes.statement: Take expectations using $\mathbb{E}\| \Delta_t \|_*^2 \le 4 \mathbb{E}\| G(z_t,\xi_t) \|_*^2 \le 4 M_*^2$ and martingale property to obtain (6.6).

nodes.name: Combine to obtain (3.10)
nodes.statement: Sum (6.3) over $t$, take supremum in $u$ and expectation; combine with (6.6) and $\mathbb{E}\| G(z_t,\xi_t) \|_*^2 \le M_*^2$ to obtain $\mathbb{E}[\sup_{u \in Z} \sum \gamma_t(z_t - u)^T g(z_t)] \le 2 + (5/2) M_*^2 \sum \gamma_t^2$.

nodes.name: Saddle point mirror SA efficiency estimate
nodes.statement: With constant stepsize $\gamma_t = 2 \theta / (M_* \sqrt{5N})$: $\mathbb{E}[\epsilon_\phi(\tilde{z}^N_1)] \le 2 \max\{\theta, \theta^{-1}\} \sqrt{10 [(D_{\omega_x,X}^2/\alpha_x) M_{*,x}^2 + (D_{\omega_y,Y}^2/\alpha_y) M_{*,y}^2] / N}$ (eq. (3.13)).
assumptions: Saddle-point setup of section 3.1 with norms and distance-generating functions on $X, Y$
Oracle bound (3.2): $\mathbb{E}\| G_x \|_{*,x}^2 \le M_{*,x}^2$, $\mathbb{E}\| G_y \|_{*,y}^2 \le M_{*,y}^2$

nodes.name: Proposition 3.2 (Large deviations for saddle point mirror SA)
nodes.statement: Under (3.16) (light-tail) and stepsizes (3.12): for any $\Omega > 1$, $\Pr\{ \epsilon_\phi(\tilde{z}^N_1) > (8 + 2\Omega) \max\{\theta,\theta^{-1}\} \sqrt{5} M_* / \sqrt{N} \} \le 2 \exp\{-\Omega\}$ (eq. (3.17)).
assumptions: Light-tail condition (3.16): $\mathbb{E}\exp\{\| G_x \|_{*,x}^2 / M_{*,x}^2\} \le e$ and analogous for $G_y$

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 3.2
nodes.statement: Using bound (6.8) (light-tail in joint norm), decompose (6.9) into a deterministic-stochastic part $\alpha_N$ and a martingale part $\beta_N$; use Markov inequality on (6.11) for $\alpha_N$ and Cramer's deviation bound (6.14) for $\beta_N$; combine and substitute (3.12).

nodes.name: Minimax stochastic problem (3.18)
nodes.statement: $\min_{x \in X} \max_{1 \le i \le m} \{ f_i(x) = \mathbb{E}[F_i(x,\xi)] \}$, with $X \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ bounded closed convex; reformulated as saddle point problem $\min_{x \in X} \max_{y \in Y} \sum_{i=1}^m y_i f_i(x)$ over the simplex $Y$.

nodes.name: Randomized oracle for minimax problem (3.20)/(3.24)
nodes.statement: $G(x,y,(\xi,\eta)) = (G_{\imath(\eta,y)}(x,\xi); -F_1(x,\xi), \ldots, -F_m(x,\xi))$ where $\imath(\eta,y)$ takes value $i$ with probability $y_i$; only one subgradient per iteration.

nodes.name: Bilinear matrix game (3.25 setup)
nodes.statement: $\min_{x \in X} \max_{y \in Y} \phi(x,y) = y^T A x + b^T x + c^T y$ with $A \in \mathbb{R}^{m \times n}$, $X, Y$ standard simplexes.

nodes.name: Randomized oracle for bilinear matrix games (3.26)
nodes.statement: $G(x,y,\xi) = (c + A_{\imath(\xi_1,y)}; -b - A^{\imath(\xi_2,x)})$ with $\xi_1, \xi_2$ independent uniform on $[0,1]$; uses one column and one row of $A$ per iteration.

nodes.name: Proposition 3.3 (Refined large-deviation bound for matrix-game randomized SA)
nodes.statement: With constant stepsize policy (3.12), for any $\Omega \ge 1$: $\Pr\{ \epsilon_\phi(\tilde{z}^N_1) > 2 M_* \sqrt{5/N} + 4 M \Omega / \sqrt{N} \} \le \exp\{-\Omega^2/2\}$ where $M = \max_j \| A_j + b \|_\infty + \max_j \| A^j + c \|_\infty$ (eq. (3.30)).
assumptions: Bilinear matrix game setup with randomized oracle (3.26)

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 3.3
nodes.statement: Using boundedness $\| G(z,\xi) \|_* \le M_*$ and the relations (3.9), (6.5), (6.7), one obtains (6.15); applying Azuma-Hoeffding's inequality to the bounded martingale difference $\zeta_t = \gamma_t (v_t - z_t)^T \Delta_t$ with $|\zeta_t| \le 4\gamma_t M$ yields (6.16); combining and substituting (3.12) gives (3.30).

nodes.name: Sublinear-time complexity for matrix games
nodes.statement: For ratio accuracy $\rho$ with confidence $1-\delta$, $N = O(1)(\ln n + \ln(1/\delta))/\rho^2$ suffices; total entries of $A$ visited is $\mathcal{M} = O(1) n(\ln n + \ln(1/\delta))/\rho^2$, much smaller than $mn$ for large $n$ and fixed $\rho$.

nodes.name: Lemma 6.1 (Telescoping prox-mapping bound)
nodes.statement: Let $\zeta_1, \ldots, \zeta_j \in \mathbb{R}^{n+m}$ and $v_{t+1} = P_{v_t}(\zeta_t)$ for $1 \le t \le j$. Then for any $u \in Z$: $\sum_{t=1}^{j} \zeta_t^T(v_t - u) \le V(v_1, u) + \tfrac{1}{2} \sum_{t=1}^j \| \zeta_t \|_*^2$.
conclusions: $\sum_{t=1}^j \zeta_t^T(v_t - u) \le V(v_1, u) + \tfrac{1}{2} \sum_{t=1}^j \| \zeta_t \|_*^2$ for all $u \in Z$

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 6.1
nodes.statement: Apply Lemma 2.1 (with $\alpha = 1$): $V(v_{t+1}, u) \le V(v_t, u) + \zeta_t^T(u - v_t) + \tfrac{1}{2}\| \zeta_t \|_*^2$; sum from $1$ to $j$ and use $V(v_{j+1}, u) \ge 0$.

nodes.name: Stochastic utility problem (numerical experiment)
nodes.statement: Test problem $\min_{x \in X} \mathbb{E}\phi(\sum_{i=1}^n (i/n + \xi_i) x_i)$ with $X$ the standard simplex, $\xi_i \sim N(0,1)$ iid, and $\phi$ piecewise linear convex with 10 breakpoints; instances L1-L4 of dimension 500-5000 are used to compare N-SA, E-SA, and SAA.

nodes.name: Stochastic max-flow problem (numerical experiment)
nodes.statement: Two-stage stochastic LP for capacity expansion: $\max_x \{ \mathbb{E}[F(x;\xi,\eta)] : \sum_{(i,j)} c_{ij} x_{ij} \le b, x_{ij} \ge 0 \}$, with $F$ the maximum $s$-$t$ flow when arc capacity is $\eta \xi_{ij}(p_{ij} + x_{ij})$; instances F1-F4.

nodes.name: SSN network planning problem (numerical experiment)
nodes.statement: Sen-Doverspike-Cosares SSN problem: $\min_x \{ \mathbb{E}[F(x,\xi)] : x \ge 0, \sum_i x_i = b \}$, with $F$ the unmet-demand quantity from a second-stage LP; $\dim x = 89$, $\dim \xi = 86$, $\sim 10^{70}$ scenarios.

nodes.name: Bilinear matrix game numerical experiment
nodes.statement: Symmetric matrices $A_{ij} = ((i+j-1)/(2n-1))^\alpha$ (E1) or $A_{ij} = ((|i-j|+1)/(2n-1))^\alpha$ (E2) of size $10^4 \times 10^4$; randomized N-SA and E-SA compared on 100 runs.

nodes.name: Polyak-Juditsky averaging asymptotic optimality
nodes.statement: Under classical SA assumptions, longer stepsizes combined with averaging of iterates yield the optimal $O(t^{-1})$ asymptotic convergence rate while being robust to stepsize choice.

nodes.name: Robbins-Monro stochastic approximation
nodes.statement: Stochastic approximation procedure for finding the root of a regression function from noisy observations; foundational scheme for SA.

nodes.name: Sample average approximation (SAA) method
nodes.statement: Generate sample $\xi_1, \ldots, \xi_N$ and approximate (1.1) by the deterministic problem (1.4); solve via a deterministic algorithm.

nodes.name: Non-Euclidean restricted memory level (NERML) method
nodes.statement: Powerful deterministic bundle-type algorithm used to solve the SAA problem (1.4) in numerical experiments.

nodes.name: Push-relabel maximum flow algorithm
nodes.statement: Used to solve the second-stage max-flow subproblem in the stochastic max-flow numerical experiment.

nodes.name: Azuma-Hoeffding inequality
nodes.statement: For a bounded martingale difference $\{\zeta_t\}$ with $|\zeta_t| \le c_t$: $\Pr\{ |\sum \zeta_t| > \lambda \} \le 2 \exp(-\lambda^2 / (2 \sum c_t^2))$. Used in the proof of Proposition 3.3.
